body.goal: Max-min fair payload throughput, i.e. the goodput of the worse-served flow. Rationale: the brief runs UDP and TCP simultaneously and asks for a scheduler ratio; because the scheduler is work-conserving, the ratio knob barely changes total delivered payload (964.8-978.3 Mbps, <1.5% across the whole range) and is essentially a fairness/guarantee knob, so 'performance' is best read as how evenly the link is shared rather than as raw aggregate (which would simply reward UDP's packet efficiency while starving TCP).
body.explanation: When both queues are backlogged the scheduler delivers UDP payload = w*979.02 Mbps and TCP payload = (1-w)*964.02 Mbps (the two constants are the UDP and TCP payload-on-wire efficiencies, 1400/1428 and 1448/1500). The two lines cross at w* = 964.02/(979.02+964.02) = 0.4961, where each flow gets ~485.7 Mbps; this is the unique point that maximizes the smaller goodput. Measured w496 gives min 485.61 Mbps, above the 482.00 Mbps min at w=0.50 and far above the 440.6/433.6 Mbps mins at w=0.45/0.55. The scheduler's work-conservation (H30/H31) means raising w above 0.496 only trades TCP throughput for UDP throughput without raising the minimum or the total, and lowering it starves UDP.
body.holds_when: Both flows are backlogged with a loss-based TCP that fills its configured share (TcpCubic/TcpNewReno/TcpBic/TcpVegas under load) and UDP's offered rate exceeds its configured share; the same ratio also sits inside the lossless work-conserving plateau when UDP is underloaded (any w >= udpRate/979.02 gives UDP loss 0 and TCP absorbing the leftover, total ~970 Mbps).
body.breaks_when: If 'performance' is redefined as aggregate payload goodput, the optimum moves to weightUdp=0.95 (UDP's higher packet efficiency adds ~6.7 Mbps over w=0.50 and ~13.5 Mbps over w=0.05, robust across variants/queue sizes per C86-C89) but starves TCP to ~48 Mbps. If TCP underfills its share (TcpBbr: at w=0.50 it took only 190 Mbps while UDP grabbed 786 Mbps), the fairness point is set by TCP's own demand and the minimum is capped near BBR's throughput regardless of w. If UDP is underloaded, every w above udpRate/979.02 is equivalent for total and loss, so the ratio only matters as a guarantee.

claims.text: With both queues backlogged the scheduler enforces UDP payload = w*979.02 Mbps and TCP payload = (1-w)*964.02 Mbps.
The scheduler is work-conserving: an underloaded UDP's unused share is given to TCP, and UDP is lossless once w >= udpRate/979.02.
UDP packets carry payload more efficiently than TCP, so aggregate goodput rises with weightUdp when both are backlogged, robust to TcpBbr, TcpNewReno, queuePkts=4 and queuePkts=1000.
The max-min fair ratio is the crossover w=0.496, giving ~485.6 Mbps to each flow and beating the 482.0 Mbps min at w=0.50.
